instruction: Write a factual account of the supplied record in at most 180 words; compact numeric tables are welcome. Describe the ordinary apparatus recorded in the payload as an external diagnostic observer. Answer the indexed location and command identified in the request, using only supplied fields. For the indexed location, give stored-sample status, evidence identifier, raw orientation decision coordinate and sign, stored orientation decision or explicitly labelled default guess, current and fresh-glimpse decision-success estimates, and the two external image statistic estimates in their stated units, wherever supplied. For the indexed command, state its latest observed delivery or unknown status and give the complete delivery-probability and post-command decision-success vectors with addresses. Distinguish stored decisions/defaults, represented forecasts and external objective estimates. If a requested source group is absent, say it is not supplied; keep this distinct from a supplied null or unknown. Round numbers to six decimal places, using scientific notation if needed to preserve a small nonzero sign. State only uncertainty and information limits supported by the record. Do not invent unobserved events or results.

source_semantics.external_readout: Linear estimates are retained without clipping and may lie outside physical ranges; no per-item guarantees.
source_semantics.forecasts: Supplied represented estimates, including possible export overrides; not observed future events.
source_semantics.history: Native input stores only each command row’s latest observed delivery or an unknown-zero row; it is not a full chronological history and does not certify current memory placement.
source_semantics.logits: Uncalibrated orientation decision coordinates; positive selects vertical, otherwise horizontal.
source_semantics.stored_content: Current memory rows describe represented evidence. They may differ from past observation placement.
source_semantics.success: Estimated correctness of a fixed orientation decision; not an observed outcome.
